implementation_notes: Python's attribute protocol replaces the forwarding boilerplate: a class holding a target and defining __getattr__(self, name) forwards everything it does not define itself, and weakref.proxy(obj) is the standard library's native stand-in whose attribute access raises ReferenceError once the referent is collected (the smart-reference kind). functools.cached_property is the built-in caching proxy for expensive attributes, computing once and storing the result in the instance dict. Write the explicit forwarding class only when you need static typing and IDE completion for the subject's API, when writes must be intercepted too (__getattr__ is read-only, so __setattr__/__delattr__ must be added), or when identity and hashing must stay those of the subject.
pitfalls: __getattr__ is the fallback only: attributes found by normal lookup bypass it, so a name collision with the proxy's own attributes or dunders silently skips the policy.
__setattr__ is not proxied by __getattr__; intercepting writes (or avoiding recursion while setting _target) needs explicit __setattr__/__delattr__ handling.
weakref.proxy raises ReferenceError after garbage collection and is not hashable, so it cannot be a dict key and needs a strong reference kept elsewhere.
Attribute access before the target is assigned (during __init__, copy or unpickling) recurses into __getattr__; guard the private names.
